# Jubilees Chapter 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Sarah Dies; Isaac Marries Rebecca; Abraham's Final Words; Jacob Blessed

---

**19:1** In the first year of the first week of the forty-second jubilee, Abraham came back and settled near Hebron — Kirjath Arba — for fourteen years.

**19:2** In the first year of the third week of that jubilee, Sarah died in Hebron.

**19:3** Abraham came to grieve for her and bury her. The angels watched to see whether he would keep his peace through the loss — whether his spirit would hold steady. He did. He was calm and composed, and in that composure he negotiated with the Hittites to find a burial place.

**19:4** God gave Abraham favor with everyone around him. He approached the Hittites gently and humbly, and they gave him the cave of Machpelah at Mamre — Ephron's field — confirming it as his permanent possession before all the Hittites living in Hebron.

**19:5** This transaction was recorded in the town register at Hebron.

**19:6** Abraham buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah at Mamre — Hebron.

**19:7** In the fourth year of that week, Abraham found a wife for Isaac: Rebecca, daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and sister of Laban.

**19:8** She became Isaac's wife. He loved her and found comfort from the grief of losing his mother.

**19:9** In the second year of the forty-second jubilee, first week, Abraham himself remarried — a woman named Keturah, from among his own household staff. (Hagar had already died before Sarah.)

**19:10** Keturah bore him six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. Dedan fathered Raguel and Nabaoth. Midian fathered Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. These were all Keturah's family.

**19:11** Abraham gave all of Keturah's sons gifts and sent them away eastward, clear of his son Isaac.

**19:12** Everything Abraham owned he left to Isaac. He gave Ishmael's sons gifts too, but sent them away from Isaac. Of all his sons, Isaac held the highest place in his heart.

**19:13** Ishmael's family and Keturah's family settled together across the eastern lands — from Paran to the borders of Babylon — in the desert regions.

**19:14** Over time they intermarried and became one people, known as Arabs and Ishmaelites.

**19:15** In the twenty-fifth year of this jubilee, Abraham was old, his eyesight was failing, and he could sense that his end was near. He called over his grandson Jacob — Rebecca had given birth to twins, Esau and Jacob: Jacob was smooth-skinned, Esau hairy and rough.

**19:16** Abraham loved Jacob; Isaac loved Esau.

**19:17** Abraham could see that Esau's conduct was wrong and that all his choices were off course — Esau simply didn't walk in God's ways.

**19:18** So Abraham called Jacob to him: "Jacob, my son!" "Yes, grandfather?" Abraham kissed him and blessed him.

**19:19** He said: "Don't marry a Canaanite woman. Go back to my father's family line — marry from my father's household."

**19:20** "God Most High will bless you — the God of your father Abraham — multiply you and make you into a great nation."

**19:21** "He will give you and your descendants this land, the land where my father lived. You will live in it and own it forever."

**19:22** Then Abraham called Isaac and said: "I'm getting old. I don't know how many days I have left — I've had a full life."

**19:23** "I'm a hundred and seventy-five years old today. Every day of my life I've kept God in front of me — sought with my whole heart to do what he wants and to walk straight in all his ways."

**19:24** "I have always hated idols and despised those who worshipped them. I've given my whole self — heart and mind — to doing the will of the one who made me."

**19:25** "He is the living God — holy, faithful, completely righteous. He doesn't play favorites, he doesn't take bribes. God is just, and he judges everyone who breaks his commands and throws away his covenant."

**19:26** "So here is my command for you, Isaac: walk upright before him. Serve him honestly and righteously. Love him with everything you have."

**19:27** "Make sure every male in your household is circumcised. Keep the covenant you've entered into with God. Follow the laws he gave your father Abraham."

**19:28** "Love what is true and righteous. Hate sin and corruption. Keep yourself clean from all defilement. Never eat blood."

**19:29** At that celebration Jacob came to visit his grandfather. Abraham loved Jacob more than all his other grandchildren. He gave Jacob the blessing reserved for the firstborn and explained what it meant to carry that responsibility.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Abraham's farewell address (vv.22-28) is rendered as a direct personal speech to Isaac. The transfer of the firstborn blessing to Jacob (v.29) is Jubilees' explanation for why Jacob — not Esau — receives it: Abraham saw Esau's character (v.17) and made a deliberate choice.*
